findings.title: XSS: unvalidated user cookie rendered unescaped in page header and card hint

cvss.justification: The `user` cookie is pulled from the Cookie header with only decodeURIComponent (src/server.ts:14-17) and rendered unescaped by bar() (src/views.ts:32-35) and the home-page card hint on every text/html response, so the sink is remotely reachable with no authentication gate (AV:N, PR:N). On its own the app only yields self-XSS (the sole cookie setter URL-encodes the username), so realistic cross-user execution requires chaining the SQLi-able /login — the only in-app path that plants an arbitrary cookie value in a victim's browser, via a CSRF-style form submission — a chained prerequisite plus victim interaction (AC:H, UI:R). Because the cookie doubles as the app's only identity, the payload overwrites the victim's session rather than inheriting it: the injected script can deface pages and capture victim input such as re-login credentials, but cannot read the victim's notes or modify server-side data, so impact is limited confidentiality and integrity, no availability, confined to the app's own origin (S:U, C:L, I:L, A:N).

findings.summary: The `user` cookie, read straight from the Cookie request header with no validation, is interpolated raw into the status bar and the home page card hint.
findings.details:
`currentUser()` (src/server.ts lines 14-17) pulls the `user` value out of the `Cookie` request header and applies only `decodeURIComponent`, with no validation against the users table, then every route passes it to `page()` as the signed-in name. Two sinks render it without any encoding: - src/views.ts lines 32-35, `bar()`: ```ts `
Demo App${ user ? `Signed in as ${user}` : "Not signed in" }
` ``` reached from `page()` at src/views.ts line 39 through `${bar(user)}`. - src/server.ts lines 21-24, the home page card hint `The notes that ${user} owns.`, which `card()` (src/views.ts lines 41-42) places into `

${hint}

`. A cookie is a client-controlled request header, so anything placed in it is rendered verbatim in a `text/html` response. The only server-side cookie setter (src/server.ts lines 72-73) encodes the username with `encodeURIComponent`, so within this app alone the vector is self-XSS; it becomes cross-user script execution as soon as any cookie-setting path exists (subdomain cookie toss, shared machine, intermediary proxy), and the code offers no defense because it never validates or encodes the header value it trusts as identity.
findings.poc: Request the home page with a crafted `user` cookie. ```http GET / HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost:3000 Cookie: user=%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E ``` The response contains `Signed in as `, so the cookie value executes as page script.
findings.impact: Anyone able to influence the victim's `user` cookie gets script execution in the application origin; at minimum a user can run script in their own session. The same unvalidated value is also used as the SQL owner filter on every query, so the entire identity model rests on an unencoded client header.

validation.reasoning: currentUser() (src/server.ts:14-17) extracts the client-controlled `user` cookie with only decodeURIComponent and no validation, and bar() (src/views.ts:32-35) plus the home-page card hint (src/server.ts:21-24 via card()) interpolate it unescaped into a text/html response, so the PoC request verbatim yields `Signed in as <script>alert(1)</script>`. The finding's self-XSS caveat is understated: the SQLi in /login (src/server.ts:71) lets `UNION SELECT` control row.username, which is then set as the `user` cookie via encodeURIComponent (round-tripped by decodeURIComponent, no protection), and a cross-site auto-submitting form POST to /login plants that cookie in a victim's browser, making the reported sink fire as real script execution. No CSP or any other mitigation exists in the app.
validation.confirmedImpact: An attacker who can influence a victim's `user` cookie — including via the app's own SQLi-able /login, which sets an arbitrary attacker-chosen cookie value — achieves arbitrary JavaScript execution in the application origin on every page, since the unvalidated cookie value is rendered unescaped in the status bar and card hint of all text/html responses.
